titulo: It's never too late to trust
resumen: Rahab welcomed the spies and acknowledged the Lord as God. Her story invites us to trust in him.

versos.texto: Joshua the son of Nun secretly sent two men out of Shittim as spies, saying, “Go, view the land, including Jericho.” They went and came into the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and slept there.

reflexion: A new chapter begins. Joshua sends two spies to scout out the land and Jericho. And the story takes an unexpected turn. The men stay in the house of Rahab, a woman who worked as a prostitute.

The story tells us what she did for a living, but it also shows us her words and her actions. In the verses that follow, Rahab hides them and acknowledges the Lord as God of heaven and earth. The New Testament names her among the ancestors of Jesus and among the examples of faith.
This is good news. God doesn't look only at where we come from. He looks at the heart that turns toward Him. Maybe today you think your past leaves you out of what God is doing.

Rahab's story tells you the opposite: it's never too late to trust in Him. If your past still hurts, talking with someone you trust or with a professional can also help you. You don't have to carry that weight alone.
dedicatoria: This letter is for you, who carry a heavy past. To God, you are not a lost cause.
oracion: Lord, thank you that your grace reaches those no one expected. Receive our past and our present today, and guide us with your light. In Jesus' name, amen.
